RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 55

An all-male panel selecting a candidate with notably less leadership credentials (teaching experience vs. a master's in educational leadership and deputy principalship) raises valid concerns about unconscious or affinity bias. However, panel composition alone does not prove discrimination.

Do not raise the panel's gender directly with the school, as this often provokes defensiveness. Instead, follow up firmly on your requested written explanation and scoring rubric. Take that documentation, along with the qualification disparity and panel composition, to your union or an employment attorney. Whether you should raise gender bias depends on what the official explanation reveals and whether you do so through formal advocacy channels.
